4.  Letter from Western  Pavement  Mayor Kendrick read letter from Western Pavement Development  praising the
  Development  exceptional leadership in the Public Works and Engineering Departments. He
  thanked Deputy Public Works Director Ciotti, City Engineer Milano and Staff for
  their service to the City and that it is greatly appreciated.

5.  Presentation to Families  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, recognized and thanked the
  RecognizingMilitaryMembers  families of military members. He reported that La Verne has a total of 74
  Military Recognition  Program")  community members who are currently serving in our military. Three
  individuals were recognized at this meeting. A mini banner was presented to
  each of the families of the military members.

  The military honorees are as follows:

  Justin  A. Balderrama  Marines
  RobertJaramilloJr.  Navy
  Warren  J. Sauceda  Army

  There was a reception after the presentation in the Large Conference Room in
  City Hall.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 20, 2019, Page 2

  Youth  of the  Year Award  Mayor Kendrick reported on the Youth of the Year Award. He stated that the
  City of La Verne recognizes that the youth in our community are tomorrow' s
  future leaders. Each year a La Verne youth that has made an outstanding
  contribution to the City during the past year is selected by the Youth and
  Family Action Committee( YFAC) to receive the La Verne Youth of the Year
  Award.

  Mayor Kendrick, on behalf of the City Council, recognized this year' s recipient
  of the La Verne Youth " Pride of La Verne" Award Vanessa Hess.
  Vanessa has been a great voice and advocate for La Verne' s youth and
  issues facing them. As a youth representative on the Youth and Family Action
  Committee, she led the group to put out information on the harms of vaping
  and the realities  of inental  health issues  in the community. Vanessa is
  mature beyond  her years as well as brave.  She continues  to be active and
  vocal on issues concerning La Verne all while being a successful student
  and participating in extracurricular activities. She has also been a leader in
  organizing volunteers for community projects/events such as maintaining
  the Veteran' s Memorial  and the City' s WinterWonderland  event.

1920 Bonita Avenue  existing Interfaith Chapel located at 1920 Bonita Avenue. The demolition was

7.  The City Council recessed at 6: 57 pm and reconvened at 7: 04 pm.

8.  Comment from Mayor Kendrick
  Mayor Kendrick thanked the audience for being at the meeting. He stated that
  at the last meeting there was disrespectful and / bad behavior, and it will not be
  tolerated. He stated that since 1906, such behavior has not occurred at a
  Council meeting. He reminded everyone to be civil and respectful and that
  disrespectful  behavior  is not acceptable  and will not be tolerated.

9.  Annual Report  and  Public  Mayor Kendrick  declared  a conflict of interest  because  he owns a business  in
  Protest"  Hearing-  Old Town  Old Town, and left the Council Chambers. Mayor Pro Tem Rosales presided
  La Verne Business  over the meeting.
  Improvement  District
  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the Annual Report and
  Public" Protest" Hearing - Old Town La Verne Business Improvement District.
  He stated that an annual public" protesY' hearing is required in order to comply
  with State Law, the Municipal Code, and By- Laws relative to the Old Town
  La Verne Business Improvement District ( OTLVBID). The City Council was
  requested  to receive and file a report of the OTLVBID  prior year  activities;
  approve the proposed  OTLVBID  2019- 2020 Annual Budget, and incorporate  it
  into the overall City Budget; and approve the re- establishment of the District
  boundaries  and assessment  formula.

  Community Development Director Scherer stated that Old Town La Verne is
  doing quite well. He reported on the events and programs sponsored by Old
  Town La Verne and the success of those events and programs.  He also
  reported  on the new events  and programs.

  Craig Walters, Old Town La Verne Board Member and business owner
  reported  on the huge success  of the Wine Walk Event and other events.  He
  also reported on the upcoming " On Tap" Beer Walk. He stated that the
  occupancy rate in Old Town La Verne is at 100 percent. He spoke about the
  strong partnership with the University of La Verne and their assistance during
  events. He spoke about forming the Old Town La Verne Association in 2018, as
  a non- profit organization comprised of business owners and Old Town
  La Verne residents. He reported that Old Town has a website. He stated it was
  created in conjunction with the City of La Verne' s Downtown Business
  Improvement District to promote businesses and the community. He also
  reported that portions of the proceeds from the Wine Walk were donated to the
  CERT organization, and so far they have donated $ 25, 000 to charitable
  organizations. He stated that they are doing quite well. He thanked the City
  Council, Community Development Director Scherer and Darleen Foye for their
  assistance.

  Council Member Carder stated that the last two years, growth in Old Town
  La Verne has been awesome and that it brings the community together. She
  thanked and commended the Old Town La Verne Association for all they do.

  Council Member Hepburn stated that Old Town La Verne has become a
  destination  point for people to visit.  He also thanked  Old Town La Verne
  Association for doing a great job.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales opened the public hearing and called for public
  comment  on this matter.

  There was  none.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 20, 2019, Page 7

  It was moved by Davis, seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried to
  receive and file a report of OTLVBID prior year activities; approve the
  OTLVBID Annual Budget, and incorporate it into the overall City Budget;
  approve  re- establishment  of the  District  boundaries  and  assessment
  formula and adopt Resolution No. 19- 30, approving the OTLVBID Annual
  Report.

11.  Upcoming Planning  City Manager Russi reported on the upcoming Planning Commission
  Commission  Vacancies  vacancies. He stated that the terms of two members of the Planning
  Commission  expire at the end of June.  Staff has received  25 applications  for
  the two vacancies, which is many more than typically seen. In the past, the
  Council would interview all applicants;  however, with the number of
  applications,  staff asked Council for direction on how to proceed.  Staff also
  provided to Council with options per Staff Report dated May 20, 2019,
  submitted  in the Agenda packet.

  Council Member Carder stated she was thrilled with the number of residents
  that want to be part of the Planning Commission, and that it showed such an
  interest and she felt strongly that they all should be given an opportunity and
  that they deserve to be heard by the City Council as to why they want to be on
  the Planning Commission. She stated she liked Option 2, to invite all the
  applicants to a special Council Meeting for a brief presentation to Council ( 3
  minutes). The City Council will then select their top 2, which will result in a final
  list for interviews.

  Council Member Hepburn concurred with Council Member Carder. He stated
  that all the applicants should be given the opportunity to address the City
  Council.  He stated that people, who really want to serve, should be heard. He
  felt that Option 2 was fair, and the whole Council would participate.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales stated that serving on the Planning Commission is a
  good segue to be on the City Council. He stated serving on the Planning
  Commission shows they are committed to the City. He also supported Option
  2.

  Council Member Davis stated that the having a robust pool of applications is
  amazing and so should the vetting process. He concurred with Council
  Member  Carder  and supported  Option 2.  He stated that full engagement is
  im portant.

  Mayor Kendrick  also supported  Option  2 and concurred  with Council  Member
  Carder. He stated that he has interviewed sixteen people for the Planning
  Commission and felt the Council has been successful in appointing the best
  person for the job.  He stated  it is important  to allow all the applicants  to be
  heard.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 20, 2019, Page 8

  It was moved by Carder, seconded by Hepburn and unanimously carried to
  support Option 2 to invite all the applicants to a special Council Meeting for a 3-
  minute presentation to City Council. The City Council wili then select their top 2
  which will result in a final list for interviews at a later date.

12.  Consider Approval  of  the  Draft  Community Development Director Scherer reported on the proposed
  Partnership Agreement  with  the  Partnership  Agreement with the La Verne Chamber of Commerce for 2019-
  La Verne Chamber  of  2020.  He stated that the La Verne Chamber  of Commerce  has submitted  an
  Commerce for 2019- 2020  updated Partnership Agreement for a 12- month term; July 1, 2019 through
  June 30, 2020. The Chamber of Commerce requested a total financial subsidy
  of$ 40, 000 over a 12- month term, in four equal quarterly payments of$ 10, 000.
  This subsidy represents a status quo amount, as compared with the prior
  agreements. The proposed Agreement also includes renewal of the Incentive-
  Subsidy Program for Business Recruitment up to$ 3, 000, and the previously
  approved line of credit.  A Chamber representative will also provide the
  Council with an update of their events

  Wayne Hurley, Chair of the La Verne Chamber of Commerce gave an update
  on the Chamber events and programs. He stated that Chamber membership
  has grown to 250.  He commended  and recognized  Leah Skinner and Brian
  McNerney for their efforts in drawing members to the Chamber.  He introduced
  incoming Chair Scott Snyder.

  Scott Snyder, Incoming Chair of the La Verne Chamber of Commerce stated he
  looked forward to working with the City of La Verne and La Verne Chamber of
  Commerce.  He thanked the Council for their support and for making La Verne
  a truly business friendly City.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales stated he and Council Member Carder have worked
  with the Chamber of Commerce for the past four years to help make the
  organization financially stable and successful. He stated that since then, the
  Chamber gets better every year promoting business and generating sales
  taxes, which makes La Verne a better place to live.

  Council Member Carder also thanked City Manager Russi and Community
  Development Director Scherer for their leadership and efforts working with the
  Chamber  of Commerce.  She also commended  the Chamber  Board,  Leah
  Skinner and Brian McNerney.

  Council Member Hepburn thanked Mayor Pro Tem Rosales and Councii
  Member Carder for their efforts working with the Chamber. He commended the
  Chamber for the increase in membership and he also thanked the Chamber
  Chair Hurley, and Incoming Chair Snyder and Leah Skinner for doing a great
  job.  He stated that La Verne businesses are the backbone that feeds our
  community and he urged residents to shop La Verne.

  Council Member Davis stated that the Chamber of Commerce and Old Town
  La Verne Association have a level of professionalism that is wonderful and it
  reflects well on our community. He stated that the Chamber of Commerce and
  Old Town  La Verne is a gem to have in our community.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, May 20, 2019, Page 9

  Mayor Kendrick also thanked Chair Hurley and Leah Skinner for doing an
  awesome job supporting the business community and the increase in
  membership. He stated that La Verne businesses support the City. He spoke
  about how people are now coming to our city to shop and eat. He suggested
  that the residents subscribe to the Chamber Newsletter.

  It was moved by Rosales, and seconded by Carder, and unanimously carried
  to approve Resolution No. 19- 29, approving the La Verne Chamber of
  Commerce' s Partnership Agreement, which includes programs and funding
  for a twelve- month term in the amount of $ 40, 000, an Incentive- Subsidy
  Program for Business  Recruitment  with  a  cost  not  to  exceed $  3, 000
  subject to Agreement  provisions,  and continuance
  of the previously
  approved  line  of credit  not  to exceed $ 10, 000, from
  July 1, 2019 through
  June 30, 2020, as recommended by the City Council Chamber Liaison
  Committee  and staff.

13.  Comments  from Council  Council Member Carder stated she was not at the last City Council meeting,
  Member Carder  but she watched it on YouTube . She stated she was very saddened by what
  she saw. She urged the residents to focus and stick to City issues and not to
  tear down City Council or staff. She stated as one way to deal with this matter,
  she would like to volunteer her time to help organizations that need help with
  volunteers. She spoke of the importance of volunteering. She stated there are
  many organizations seeking volunteers, like the Friends of the La Verne
  Library. She urged the community to move forward and to work together for
  the betterment of the City.

  information regarding their draft employee employment contract. He urged

  Sherry Best, President of the La Verne Historical Society reported on the

  Joanne Butler, Hillcrest Terrace, thanked the City Council for the marvelous

  Lisa, La Verne resident, spoke about her concerns  about the health hazards to
